title.en: One-dimensional arrays, linear and binary search

hook.en: Fifty variables m1, m2 … m50 would be a nightmare. An array keeps all fifty under one name, and an index picks out each one.

objectives.en: Declare, create and initialise one-dimensional arrays
Traverse an array with a loop using length
Search an array with linear search and binary search

narration.en: Fifty variables m1, m2 … m50 would be a nightmare. An array keeps all fifty under one name, and an index picks out each one.

body.en: An array is a fixed-size collection of elements of the same type stored in contiguous memory. int[] m = new int[5]; creates five ints, all 0; int[] p = {3, 8, 1}; creates and initialises. Elements are numbered from 0, so the last index is m.length − 1 (length is a field, not a method). Using an index outside 0 … length − 1 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at run time. An array variable holds a reference to the array object.

body.en: Linear search checks the elements one by one from the start until the key is found or the array ends: it works on any array and needs up to n comparisons. Binary search works only on a sorted array: it compares the key with the middle element and continues in the left or right half, so it needs at most about log2 n + 1 comparisons (10 for 1000 elements, 20 for a million).

steps.en: While low <= high, find mid = (low + high) / 2
If a[mid] equals the key, report mid and stop
If a[mid] is less than the key, set low = mid + 1
If the loop ends, report that the key is not found

explanation.en: Each pass halves the range [low, high]; when the range becomes empty the key is absent.
